text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
- The Western Defence Union fears that Norwegian defence systems will break down because of computer problems in year 2000. The alliance has sent a warning to Defence Minister Joergen Kosmo.

- So far this year shares on the Oslo bourse have risen on average by nearly 20 percent. Spain and Switzerland have the strongest bourses in the world at the moment, while the Oslo bourse is ranked as ninth.

- Food-based conglomerate Orkla ASA is sceptical to the proposed merger between Norway's largest insurer Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Orkla is afraid Christiania's network of bank branches will be to expensive to run.

- Saga Petroleum ASA posted operating results of 1.38 billion crowns for the first quarter of 1997, 60 percent up from the same year-ago period. Increased production and higher oil prices were the main reason for the rise.

- Trade and Industry Minister Grete Knudsen met members of Chilean fishing organisation CONAPACH on Thursday. The minister faced criticism for not having met with Chilean fishermen when she visited the country a short time ago. CONAPACH is strongly opposed to plans of Norway's Aker RGI to fish in the 20-mile Chilean fishing zone with its new vessel American Monarch.
